fidelity: F2a — Lumped Network Thermal Transient (supply/return ODE)
source: Lund, J.W. & Toth, A.N. (2021) Direct Utilization of Geothermal Energy 2020 Worldwide Review, Geothermics 90, 101915; Lund, J.W., Freeston, D.H. & Boyd, T.L. (2011) Direct utilization of geothermal energy 2010 worldwide review, Geothermics 40(3) 159-180; Frederiksen, S. & Werner, S. (2013) District Heating and Cooling, Studentlitteratur.

unit.name: Generic Direct-Use Geothermal District Heating Plant (Lund & Toth 2021 typical)

T_geo_source.note: Geothermal production-well wellhead temperature (Lund & Toth 2021 direct-use median 50-90 C)

T_geo_reinject_min.note: Minimum geothermal reinjection temperature; cascade use drives this low to maximise extraction

T_supply_setpoint.note: Network supply temperature set point delivered to consumers

T_return_nominal.note: Nominal network return temperature from consumers

V_supply.note: Lumped water volume of supply side of network (pipes + headers + thermal capacitance)

V_return.note: Lumped water volume of return side of network

rho_water.note: Water density at ~65 C (IAPWS-IF97, Wagner & Pruss 2002)

cp_water.note: Specific heat of liquid water near 60-70 C (CRC Handbook / IAPWS); hardcoded per F2 spec

UA_supply.note: Supply-pipe distribution heat-loss coefficient to ground (overall UA of buried supply network)

UA_return.note: Return-pipe distribution heat-loss coefficient to ground

T_ground.note: Mean ground/soil temperature around buried pipes

f_cascade.note: Fraction of geothermal return heat recovered by cascade users (greenhouses/aquaculture) before reinjection (Lund & Toth 2021)

Q_boiler_max.note: Peak gas/biomass boiler capacity to top up supply temperature on cold days
